hdr="some text"

-- Alias `hd` to `l` via `hd hdr` — `hd` resolves to the text slice, not the
-- built-in list head. Aliases are not allowed on `R`-fns; `hd` is the canonical
-- form, `l` is the canonical shape.
hd hdr:t>t;hd hdr

-- Alias `len` to `n` via `len hdr` — `len` resolves to the text length,
-- not the built-in list-length builtin. Aliases are not allowed on `R`-fns;
-- `n` is the canonical form.
len hdr:t>n;len hdr

-- Alias `flt` to `ok` via `flt hdr` — `flt` resolves to the text filter,
-- not the built-in list-filter builtin. Aliases are not allowed on `R`-fns;
-- `ok` is the canonical form.
flt hdr:t>R n t;flt hdr

-- Alias `cat` to `l` via `cat hdr s` — `cat` resolves to the text join,

```python
import ilo

my_list = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

# Negative indexing
negative_indexed_list = my_list[-3:]  # Equivalent to my_list[-1:-2]

```

In this example:
- `my_list[-3:]` slices the list starting from the third element (index -3) to the end.
- `my_list[:-3]` slices the list starting from the beginning (index 0) to the third element (index -3).
